purpose: Adds a configurable budget-based review system that adapts review depth to PR diff size: full review under the summary threshold, summary/critical-patterns-only mode at 500+ lines, and a split-recommendation banner for 1000+ line PRs. It threads a ReviewBudgetMode through new types, zod schema, YAML/env config wiring across action and app, the prompt builder banners, and applies the split banner centrally in verifyReviewResult.
riskRationale: Well-structured and well-tested, but the diff-size metric (raw patch line count) can over-trigger summary mode on ordinary PRs and under-count GitHub-truncated or binary patches on exactly the very large PRs #238 targets; the summary/split banner text partially conflicts with the strict JSONL output contract parseJsonlFile enforces; the feature is enabled by default, silently changing review depth for 500-1000 line PRs; and reviewBudget is a new required field on ReviewConfig (breaking type change).
breakingChanges: ReviewConfig.reviewBudget is now a required field (breaking type change for external consumers of the lib that construct ReviewConfig/AgentConfig literals without spreading DEFAULT_CONFIG)
Review depth for PRs with 500-1000 diff lines changes from full to summary-only by default (enabled: true)

text: The PR cleanly implements a budget-based review mode (full/summary/split) with proper types, schema validation, config wiring across action and app, prompt banners, a centrally-applied split banner in verifyReviewResult, and solid unit tests. The main concerns are semantic: totalDiffLines counts raw patch text rather than actual added/deleted lines (over-triggering summary on ordinary PRs while undercounting the largest PRs it targets), the budget banner is injected into every per-batch sub-agent prompt in multi-batch mode, the banner text partially contradicts the JSONL output contract, and the feature ships enabled-by-default with a required config field (a breaking type change).

reasoning: The architecture is sound and the tests are solid, but the diff-size metric, per-batch banner injection, banner-vs-JSONL-contract conflict, missing failure-path banner, required-field breaking change, and enabled-by-default behavior change should be addressed before merge so large-PR reviews don't silently lose findings or change depth unexpectedly. All are straightforward, low-risk fixes.

message: determineBudgetMode is simple, well-documented, and safely falls back to 'full' when reviewBudget is missing or disabled (the `if (!budget?.enabled) return 'full'` guard), so the feature degrades gracefully to existing behavior.

validateConfig rounds and clamps budget thresholds to positive integers and forces splitThreshold >= summaryThreshold, mirroring the tokenBudget validation pattern so malformed YAML can't produce inverted or degenerate modes.

Applying the split banner centrally in verifyReviewResult guarantees it is prepended on every successful result path (single-batch, batch+synthesis success, synthesis-failure fallback, parse-failure fallback) and is applied last so reachability/meta-verification edits aren't clobbered.

Budget-mode tests cover real engine flows end-to-end: mode selection at thresholds, disabled budget falling back to 'full', custom thresholds, multi-file diff aggregation, and banner presence/absence.

totalDiffLines is computed from the raw patch text (f.patch.split('\n').length), which counts hunk headers, context lines, and diff metadata — inflating counts so ordinary medium PRs can cross the default 500-line summaryThreshold early and silently lose line-by-line review. Conversely, GitHub's patch field is null for binary files and omitted/truncated for very large files, so the biggest PRs (#238's target) undercount to 0 and stay in 'full' mode, defeating the feature's purpose. ChangedFile's additions/deletions are always present and accurate.
suggestion: Compute totalDiffLines from the per-file additions + deletions (already populated on ChangedFile) instead of splitting the raw patch text, so the metric matches the documented 'diff lines' semantics and the banner's reported count.

message: In multi-batch mode (files.length > batchSize), the whole-PR budgetMode and totalDiffLines are forwarded to every per-batch buildReviewPrompt call. Each small batch — containing only up to batchSize files — is told 'This PR has ~N lines' and 'Do NOT perform a line-by-line review', which over-restricts depth for batches that could be fully reviewed, and in split mode every batch is also asked to emit a split recommendation. This degrades the per-batch sub-agent reviews the pipeline relies on for large PRs.
suggestion: Apply the budget banner only on the single-batch path and the final synthesis/summary prompt, not to each per-batch sub-agent prompt; pass undefined for budgetMode/totalDiffLines in the batch loop (engine.ts:418-433) or recompute them per batch from that batch's files.

message: The summary/split banners instruct the model to 'Skip line-by-line review', 'Provide a summary-level assessment', and 'provide a recommendation to split this PR', but the prompt's Output Format: JSON Lines section (builder.ts:189) still requires structured issue/strength/verdict lines that parseJsonlFile consumes. A model following the banner may emit prose or few/no structured findings, so parseJsonlFile returns an empty result and issues are silently dropped. The split recommendation is also redundant — the engine already prepends it programmatically via applyBudgetModeBanner.
suggestion: Reword the banners to preserve the JSONL contract: still require structured issue/strength lines restricted to critical patterns (security, breaking changes, API misuse), and remove the 'provide a recommendation to split' prose since the engine injects it itself.

message: The single-batch early-return failure paths (runOpenCode failure at engine.ts:332-337 and parse failure at engine.ts:371-376) return the bare empty result without calling verifyReviewResult, so the 'Large PR Detected' split banner is never prepended on exactly the scenario #238 targets — an oversized PR that times out or fails yields a plain 'Review execution failed' result with no guidance to split the PR.
suggestion: Apply the budget banner on the early-return failure paths too, e.g., return this.applyBudgetModeBanner(r, budgetMode, totalDiffLines) in both single-batch failure returns so large-PR guidance still reaches users when the review itself fails.

message: reviewBudget is added as a required (non-optional) field on ReviewConfig, which is a breaking change for any external consumer of the published lib that constructs ReviewConfig/AgentConfig literals without spreading DEFAULT_CONFIG. It is also internally inconsistent: determineBudgetMode defensively uses budget?.enabled (expecting undefined) while applyBudgetModeBanner accesses this.config.review.reviewBudget.splitThreshold unguarded — the two should agree. Compare with tokenBudget, which is correctly optional.
suggestion: Make reviewBudget optional (reviewBudget?: ReviewBudgetConfig) so determineBudgetMode's existing `if (!budget?.enabled) return 'full'` guard handles the unset case, add optional chaining in applyBudgetModeBanner, and keep the action/app wiring and DEFAULT_CONFIG as-is.
suggestionCode:
/** Budget-based review configuration for large PRs */
  reviewBudget?: ReviewBudgetConfig;

message: The feature is enabled by default (enabled: true in DEFAULT_CONFIG.review.reviewBudget and in the zod schema default), so this silently changes existing behavior for all users on upgrade: PRs in the 500-1000 diff-line range that previously received full line-by-line reviews now get summary-only critical-pattern reviews with no opt-in. That is a review-quality regression for mid-size PRs and should either default to disabled or be prominently documented as a behavior change.
suggestion: Default the feature to enabled: false so existing users must opt in, or add an explicit upgrade/behavior-change note in README/CHANGELOG describing the reduced review depth for 500-1000 line PRs.

message: The app's env-var path reads REVIEW_BUDGET_SUMMARY_THRESHOLD and REVIEW_BUDGET_SPLIT_THRESHOLD via parseEnvInt with no clamping or ordering validation (unlike the action path, which sanitizes through lib validateConfig). REVIEW_BUDGET_SUMMARY_THRESHOLD=0 makes totalDiffLines >= 0 always true, so every PR runs in summary mode; a splitThreshold below summaryThreshold silently makes summary mode unreachable; and parseEnvInt tolerates trailing garbage ('100x' -> 100).
suggestion: Clamp both thresholds to a minimum of 1 and enforce splitThreshold >= summaryThreshold when constructing reviewBudget from env vars, mirroring lib/src/config.ts:200-215.

message: ReviewBudgetConfigSchema.default({}) in ReviewConfigSchema returns the literal '{}' without re-parsing it through the object schema, so the inner field defaults (enabled: true, thresholds) are never applied. Any consumer validating via AgentConfigSchema that omits reviewBudget gets { enabled: undefined }, which silently disables budget mode. The action/app bypass this by building the config manually, but the schema default is misleading.
suggestion: Use .default(ReviewBudgetConfigSchema.parse({})) so the object-level default is re-parsed and applies field defaults, or drop the object-level default and rely on per-field defaults.

message: ReviewBudgetConfigSchema has no .refine() enforcing splitThreshold >= summaryThreshold, unlike TokenBudgetConfigSchema which does. The manual validateConfig in lib/src/config.ts clamps this, but the zod AgentConfigSchema path does not, so inverted thresholds pass silently through that validation path. The two validation paths should behave consistently.
suggestion: Add a .refine() to ReviewBudgetConfigSchema (mirroring TokenBudgetConfigSchema) enforcing splitThreshold >= summaryThreshold.

message: The documented mode boundaries don't match the implementation. The README says '< 500 lines: full', '500–1000 lines: summary', and '> 1000 lines: split', but determineBudgetMode uses >= comparisons (engine.ts:117-118), so exactly 1000 lines selects split mode and exactly 500 selects summary mode. Documentation and behavior are off-by-one at the boundary, and the tests use 600 lines rather than the exact 500/1000 boundaries.
suggestion: Align the README to the implementation ('>= 500' for summary, '>= 1000' for split), or change the comparisons to strict '>' if the documented ranges are intended; add boundary tests at exactly 500 and 1000 lines to pin the semantics.

message: verifyReviewResult gained two new parameters (budgetMode, totalDiffLines) but its JSDoc was not updated to document them, and at 7 positional parameters the signature is hard to read and easy to misuse at call sites (the synthesis-failure fallback already passes a bare `undefined` placeholder at engine.ts:603).
suggestion: Document the new params in the JSDoc and consider refactoring verifyReviewResult (and applyBudgetModeBanner) to take a single options object for readability and argument-order safety.

message: buildReviewPrompt has grown to 10 positional parameters, and the engine tests index the mocked call by position (e.g. mockBuildReviewPrompt.mock.calls[0][8]). Every future signature addition is a silent-break risk at call sites and hurts readability.
suggestion: Refactor the trailing optional params (linterResults, budgetMode, totalDiffLines) into the existing ReviewPromptOptions object so call sites are self-documenting and positional-argument fragility is reduced.

message: buildReviewPrompt returns early when a custom review prompt file is configured (inputs.reviewPromptFile), so the budget-mode banner is never injected for users who set reviewPromptFile. Budget adaptation is silently disabled for those users even though reviewBudget is enabled globally.
suggestion: Append the budget banner to the custom prompt too (e.g., after reviewPromptExtra), or document that custom prompt files bypass the budget banner.

message: In summary/split modes the full per-file diffs are still embedded in every prompt via buildPRContextString and all batches still run; only the instruction banner changes (builder.ts:142-145). Since input tokens and per-batch runtime are unchanged, the 'budget' does not actually reduce context consumption — the timeout/context-overflow risk that motivated #238 is only partially mitigated (shorter model output). This was an explicit maintainer decision, but the tradeoff is undocumented.
suggestion: Consider dropping the embedded per-file diffs from batch prompts in summary/split modes (or sharply lowering the truncation cap) and instructing the model to read files with the read tool, or at minimum document that budget modes do not reduce input tokens.

message: For incremental (follow-up) reviews triggered by previousHeadSha, totalDiffLines is computed from the full PR files rather than the delta being re-reviewed. On a large PR this forces summary/split mode for a small delta, and the budget banner ('Do NOT perform a line-by-line review') directly contradicts the prompt's 'Incremental Review (Delta Changes)' directive to focus on the new commits, degrading follow-up review quality.
suggestion: Skip budget-mode adaptation (or compute the count from the delta context) when previousHeadSha is provided, since incremental reviews target only the new commits.
